verdict: Smurfit Westrock's net sales rose 2% to $8.2B, but what it called unprecedented freight and energy cost inflation cut gross profit 8% and net income fell — the company is pushing through price increases it expects to more than offset those costs into 2027.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: net sales of $8,161M vs $8,003M a year ago

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Paperboard, corrugated and consumer packaging in the U.S., Canada and Mexico — the biggest region, with adjusted EBITDA of $760M at a 15.6% margin.

segments.name: Europe, MEA and APAC
segments.note: Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific — sales were flat as containerboard price increases passed through with a lag against rising energy costs; adjusted EBITDA was $379M.

segments.name: Latin America
segments.note: Central and South America and the Caribbean — the smallest but highest-margin region, with adjusted EBITDA of $126M at a 21.4% margin.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative expenses — down from $963M a year ago.

opex.name: Impairment & restructuring
opex.note: Impairment and restructuring costs as the combined company reshapes its mill and converting footprint.

otherDetail: Below operating profit: $174M of net interest expense, plus $8M of pension and postretirement non-service income, minus $7M of other expense, gives net other expense of $173M.
footerNote: Net income was $219M; noncontrolling interests took a $3M loss, so net income attributable to common shareholders was $222M.

takeaways.title: Sales grew, profit shrank
takeaways.text: Net sales rose 2% to $8,161M, but cost of goods sold rose faster — gross profit fell 8% to $1,440M — as freight, energy and other input costs surged.

takeaways.title: Cost inflation is the story
takeaways.text: Management expects to absorb about $700M of extra freight and energy costs alone in 2026, and cut its full-year adjusted EBITDA estimate to about $4.7B. Price increases already announced are meant to more than offset this, mostly landing in 2027.

takeaways.title: Still investing heavily
takeaways.text: Capital expenditures — money spent on buildings and equipment — were $514M in the quarter, against $874M of operating cash flow, and the company paid a quarterly dividend of $0.4523 per share.

oneTimers: $26M of impairment and restructuring costs in the quarter, as the company continues reshaping the combined Smurfit Kappa / WestRock footprint.
